None of the standing rules impose a mandatory Kelvin-first nomination floor that fires when the compiler's output contains zero Kelvin-class stubs for currently-failing cables. This structural compiler priority bias — nominating CAN/I2C instead of failing Kelvin pairs — will not self-correct via absorber-bypass alone if the compiler never generates the stubs to bypass.

4. NON-KELVIN UNCONNECTED SURPLUS (Rule 28 fires): unconnected=4, Kelvin-class unconnected nets in failing_reasons = 3 (/SENSEC1_HI, /SENSEC1_LO, /SENSEC2_HI), so N_non_kelvin = 4 - 3 = 1. ESCALATION SUMMARY: This round has four concurrent conditions that independently require escalation or halt — M_actual undercount, total absorption with kelvin fail, compiler miss (new), and non-Kelvin unconnected identity unknown. scorer_penalty.rationale: Round 62 demonstrates that kelvin_unrouted=1 is a metric undercount (M_actual=2 per Rule 29). Even before the calibration is fixed, raising the per-unit penalty from 1000 to 1500 increases the objective cost of any round where the metric reports even one failing Kelvin pair, making the objective function more aggressively penalize Kelvin failures relative to the DRC and length terms. At M_actual=2 with the corrected count this yields 2*1500=3000 vs the current 1*1000=1000 — a 3x effective increase in Kelvin pressure on the objective ranking, which better reflects the true safety-gate severity of leaving a current-sense pair unrouted.

manager_rule: After each round, derive the set K_miss = {N : cable index N has at least one of /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines'} MINUS {N : at least one of /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO appears in the stub compiler's output 'nets' list for that round}. If K_miss is non-empty, log 'kelvin_compiler_miss' with fields: (a) round number, (b) K_miss (the set of cable indices whose failing Kelvin nets received zero compiler nominations), (c) the full compiler output nets list, (d) n_stubs, absorbed, trimmed_spurs, removed_orphans. On the immediately following round, the compiler MUST unconditionally include at least one /SENSEC{N}_HI stub and at least one /SENSEC{N}_LO stub for EVERY cable index N in K_miss, treating these as priority-override nominations that bypass normal priority-score filtering — i.e., these stubs are emitted regardless of the compiler's accumulated priority weights or any decay state for those nets. Additionally, the absorber MUST NOT apply merge, trim, or spur-removal logic to any stub whose target net is /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO for N in K_miss — these mandatory Kelvin stubs must be forwarded to FR intact. If K_miss persists non-empty for 3 consecutive rounds with mandatory Kelvin-override stubs active, escalate immediately as 'persistent_kelvin_compiler_miss' for inspection of the compiler priority model and any compiler_excluded_nets entries that may be suppressing Kelvin net nomination, halting FR dispatch pending human review. This rule addresses the gap between Rules 19/26 (which handle absorber disposal of EMITTED Kelvin stubs) and Rules 30/31 (which exclude stale non-Kelvin nets): it fires when the compiler never nominates the failing Kelvin nets at all, a condition the absorber-bypass and exclusion-list mechanisms cannot correct on their own.
